- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from recent peak), model often overshoots in short-term forecast — cap next-period forecast at 1–2% below peak to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model frequently overestimates upward momentum — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment swings >0.3.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >+3% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% for next period unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was negative 3–5 days ago, model often misses correction — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
